- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above peak or align with 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 1.0) and price is trending up, model overestimates — apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +1.5 to -1.5 within 5 days), model exhibits lag — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and smooth transitions.
- Mean reversion is triggered if forecast deviates > 10% from 30-day moving average — bring forecast back to average within 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period — reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 3–7% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment is volatile and price is flat, model tends to overpredict — apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day EWMA) to forecast.
